people.name: Mordecai
people.description: Benjamite Jew at the Persian court who dreams of the two serpents and prays for Israel.
people.identity_note: 4:18 ('He prayed') identifies Mordecai by context of 4:17; 10:7 ('Haman and me') is Mordecai speaking. Genealogy in 1:1 repeats Hebrew Esther 2:5 (Jair, Shimei, Kish).

people.name: Shimei
people.identity_note: Chain mirrors Hebrew Esther 2:5; whether Shimei/Kish are immediate or remote ancestors is debated; existing ids shimei-est2 / kish-est2 used exactly as for Hebrew Esther.

people.name: Esther
people.description: Jewish queen who prays for deliverance and approaches the king.
people.identity_note: Her prayer runs 4:29-4:47. Her father is named Aminadab in Greek 2:7/2:15/9:29 (not addition text; = Abihail of Hebrew Esther), so not recorded here.

people.name: Ahasuerus
people.description: Persian king who issues the decrees of Additions B and E.
people.identity_note: The LXX Greek of Esther (incl. the additions) calls the king Artaxerxes; this WEB text renders him 'Ahasuerus' throughout, including inside the bracketed additions. Same king as in Hebrew Esther, so mapped to existing id 'ahasuerus'. In 5:1 and 10:6 he is 'the king' within addition text.

people.name: Haman
people.description: Royal favourite whose plot against the Jews is described in the decrees and Mordecai's dream.
people.identity_note: Called 'the Bougean' in 1:1 and 'a Macedonian ... alien from the blood of the Persians' in 8:13 (Addition E); parentage restated in 8:13.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.description: King of Babylon who carried Mordecai's people captive.

people.name: Jeconiah
people.description: King of Judea taken captive to Babylon.

people.name: Gabatha
people.description: Royal chamberlain and eunuch who plotted against the king and was exposed by Mordecai.
people.identity_note: Addition A's plot parallels Hebrew Esther 2:21-23 (Bigthan and Teresh); Gabatha is probably the Greek form of Bigthan(a), but the Greek book presents Addition A as an earlier, separate episode (and repeats the plot at 2:21-23 with unnamed chamberlains), so not mapped to 'bigthan'. Reviewer may merge.

people.name: Tharrha
people.description: Royal chamberlain and eunuch who plotted against the king with Gabatha.
people.identity_note: Probably = Teresh of Hebrew Esther 2:21 (existing id 'teresh'); not mapped for the same reason as Gabatha. A Tharrha also appears among the seven chamberlains in Greek 1:10 (not addition text).

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch invoked in the prayers ('God of Abraham').

people.name: Ptolemeus
people.description: Ptolemaic king in whose fourth year the Greek Esther was brought to Egypt.
people.identity_note: Which Ptolemy (VIII, XII or XIV) is debated. 'Ptolemeus and Cleopatra' reign jointly; no spouse link recorded because the text does not state their relation.

people.name: Cleopatra
people.description: Ptolemaic queen co-reigning with Ptolemy in the colophon's date.

people.name: Dositheus
people.description: Self-described priest and Levite who brought the Purim letter to Egypt.

people.name: Ptolemeus
people.description: Son of Dositheus who accompanied him with the Purim letter.

people.name: Lysimachus
people.description: Man in Jerusalem said to have translated the Purim letter.

people.name: Ptolemeus
people.identity_note: Not the king; the text gives no sign he is the son of Dositheus, so kept separate.

notes: WEB ESG is a translation of the full Greek Esther in 10 chapters, with the additions merged into the Hebrew chapter/verse frame (not the Vulgate 10:4-16:24 numbering). Addition limits: A = bracketed first part of 1:1 (Mordecai's dream and the eunuchs' plot; the text after ']' is Hebrew 1:1); B = bracketed second part of 3:13 (Ahasuerus's decree against the Jews); C = 4:18-4:47, bracketed (prayer of Mordecai 4:18-27, narrative 4:28, prayer of Esther 4:29-47); D = 5:1-5:2 (expanded Greek account of Esther before the king; NOT bracketed in WEB and blended with Hebrew 5:1-2 content); E = bracketed part of 8:13 (decree rehabilitating the Jews); F = 10:4-10:14, bracketed (interpretation of the dream, 10:4-13, and colophon, 10:14). Verses 4:6, 9:5 and 9:30 are absent from the WEB numbering. Verses 1:1, 3:13 and 8:13 contain both addition and Hebrew-parallel text; the refs there point to names inside the bracketed part. Esther's two maids (5:1) are not recorded as individuals. King name: LXX 'Artaxerxes', WEB 'Ahasuerus'; mapped to existing 'ahasuerus'. Parent links whose names repeat (three different Ptolemies) carry a 'new_id' field to disambiguate.
